name: Petra Jones
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember selling my last copy to the author's enemy.” Tuesday often includes a stop at the public road outside the Port of Asphalt, where Petra can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: I sold out of copies until the real man stood in the doorway. Now I ask who wants to read and who wants to stare.
appearance: Petra has short sandy hair and a marked widow's peak, a narrow face with an expressive upper lip, and a favorite piece of clothing, a brown corduroy jacket. It usually goes with a narrow brass watch set a little fast. When somebody else has the floor, Petra looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry.
personality: Petra reads little signals of discomfort very accurately and has an unfortunate habit of overruling people for their own good. The friends who say stop are the ones Petra trusts most.
agenda: To keep the real resident from becoming a shop exhibit.
family: Miguel Grant is Petra’s stepsibling. Petra leaves the first voice message. Miguel calls back when there is finally a little privacy. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *Salt in the pockets*, Miguel says, “I didn't recognize my own coat clean. My kid found it by the spot where I'd held her crayons.”
connections: Stevie Rose. A bookseller guarding a customer's privacy finds a host for a quieter discussion.
